_: THE SHOP'S PALETTES, AS DATA. The seller changes these often, so they are not spelled out in the stylesheet any more - build_db.py writes the chosen one into site/src/styles/theme.css and global.css imports it. Changing the whole shop is one word in business.config.json: "theme". Add a preset by copying a block; every preset must define every token, because there is no fallback and a missing one is an invisible colour.
_plate_wall:
The background of the image panels and product tiles ONLY. It must be the EXACT cream the mockups are photographed on, rgb(237,234,227) / #edeae3, on EVERY theme - light or dark.

CORRECTED 28 Oct, and the previous advice here was wrong. It used to say: match the cream on a light theme, but on a dark theme set it near the page colour so the print reads as a lit panel on a dark wall. That cannot work. The cream is baked into the photograph - it is the wall the print was shot against - so a dark panel does not darken the picture, it just puts a hard cream rectangle inside a dark box with a visible edge. The seller spotted it within an hour of the black theme going live: 'around product image is creamy colour, it looked nicer before'. It had looked right before because gallery-cream's panel was #f6f4ef, near enough the photograph to hide the seam.

So: cream panels on a black page, which is what a gallery does anyway. The only way to make this token dark is to re-shoot every mockup on a dark wall.
_scheme: light or dark. It sets color-scheme, so native form controls and scrollbars follow the palette instead of fighting it.

ink-black.label: Ink black - black page, pure white type, no warm tint

paper-white.label: Paper white - white page, black type

gallery-cream.label: Gallery cream - the mockups' own background, no seam

plaster-pink.label: Plaster pink - warm gallery pink, claret accent

_ink_black_note:
NEUTRAL GREYS ONLY IN THIS PRESET. Every ink was warm - #f4f3f0 for type, #c2bfb9 and #8d8a85 for the quieter greys - and the papers carried a faint violet tint. Individually invisible; across a whole page it reads as cream, which is what the seller saw and asked to be white. Corrected 28 Oct to pure #ffffff type on #000000 with grey steps that have equal R, G and B.

THE ONE TOKEN THAT STAYS WARM IS plate-wall, #edeae3, and it must. That is not a design choice, it is the colour the mockups were photographed against - see _plate_wall. Neutralising it brings back the visible seam around every product image.
